messages:
alice: Quick triage: ran profiling against canary runtime. Observed ~12% tail latency regression for streaming requests after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. Short summary: more frequent kernel swaps and smaller effective batch sizes when partial-decode streaming chunks hit the queue. Can we triage?
ben: Confirmed. Repro steps: 1) run streaming clients (avg req len 64 tokens, chunk every 8). 2) peak load shows batch sizes drop to 1-3. Logs show `kernel_switch_ms` spikes. Sharing repro script.
carla: Flamegraphs show when batch_size < 4 we fall back to scalar path (+~2.5-3ms/token). Partial-decode scheduling is creating many micro-batches. Also seeing KV cache churn because tiny decodes re-materialize per-chunk state.
dave: KV notes: recent memory-pressure patch shortened eviction windows; hot KV shards aren't sticky so streaming micro-batches cause reloads (~0.8ms/request) and extra variance.
megan: Two levers to test: (A) queue partition: streaming lane aims to form decent batches (min_batch=4) with short greedy wait (6ms) before flush; (B) token budget: set streaming token_budget_target=32 so several tiny chunks can coalesce. Might reduce kernel swaps.
ben: Also think about soft-priority fairness: expedite first chunk of streaming to preserve first-chunk latency, but allow subsequent streaming chunks to join batch_queue for >=min_batch or wait window (10ms). Pseudo:
```
if is_streaming and is_first_chunk:
  expedite_queue.push(req)
else:
  batch_queue.push(req)
# flush when batch_size>=min_batch or age>window_ms
```
carla: Kernel selector currently runs per-request, causing switches. If we piggyback kernel decision on model-profile + token_length hints (or sticky kernel per-session for short windows) we can avoid many swaps.
dave: For KV, propose sticky-KV pinning: mark session hot on first access and keep shards pinned for N ms (e.g., 200ms sliding). That should cut reloads for rapid partial decodes.
alice: Let's define two AB arms for canary:
A) min_batch=4, greedy_wait=6ms, token_budget=32, stickyKV=200ms, prefetch_kernel_hint=true
B) min_batch=2, greedy_wait=3ms, token_budget=16, stickyKV=50ms, prefetch_kernel_hint=false
Metrics: p50/p95/p99 streaming latency, kernel_switch_rate, avg_batch_size, kv_miss_rate, first-chunk latency, cpu tail.
megan: I'll wire flags and run a 2h AB on canary (slice=5%). Will add kernel_switch_cost histogram tagged by is_streaming and batch_size.
ben: Watch tail CPU when min_batch increases — we might increase queueing and risk SLOs. If queue_age>threshold, flush immediately (adaptive backoff).
carla: Micro-opt: when flushing tiny streaming batches (<min_batch) publish a lightweight 'prefetch kernel' hint to the next worker so it can pre-select kernel early and reduce per-request kernel_select overhead.
alice: Add prefetch_kernel_hint toggle to arm A. Megan include that.
megan: Running now. infra-bot: deploy canary/runtime/2026-06-15 18:12 rolled out to canary cluster (slice=5%). I'll post results + perf traces after the run.
ben: If kernel_switch_rate drops and avg_batch_size rises we're good. If KV miss rate stays high we'll iterate on stickyKV values.
dave: I'll prototype sticky-KV pinning and expose telemetry for pinned_shard_hitrate.
carla: I'll prototype kernel hint RPC and a small change to kernel selector to prefer session-affinity within 200ms windows.
alice: Follow-ups: megan to post results, carla to prototype kernel hint, dave to add sticky-KV. Reconvene after 2h run. :thumbsup:
